svg.title: UMSH messenger on the LilyGO T-LoRa Pager, mockups
svg.text: 480×222 landscape, no touch. Side wheel with press, 31-key keyboard. Screens drawn at 2×.

g.text: On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: On the right edge. Turn moves focus. In an active text field it moves the cursor: a
character per click, a word at a time when spun fast. Press selects, or ends typing.
Open in lists. In a text field: start typing, then Send.
Always text. Typing activates the focused field, or a list’s filter. Never commands.
The arrow key under the wheel. Erases while a field is active; everywhere else it is Back.
Not on this face, and not used for navigation.
Chats, Peers and Device sit on a rail beside the top-level lists. Back moves focus onto it.
Typing on any list filters it. Typing a name is how a new chat starts.
Focus a message with the wheel and press it. A link in a message is its first action.
Body text is 20 px, about 2.3 mm on this panel, and nothing is under 16 px.
When a list or the history continues, its last row is cut by the screen edge. No scroll bars.
Field states carry the controls: a cursor means keys type; no cursor means Backspace is Back.
The radio is built in, so the strip shows only the device name, time, phone link, GNSS and battery.
Enter always belongs to the composer.

g.text: On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: Home. Two lines per chat; the fifth row is clipped, so the list plainly goes on. A draft shows in place of the last message. The rail
Letters typed on a list start a filter, active at once. Enter opens the tinted top result; press moves into the results. Groups follow

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: Active: heavier border and a cursor, here inserting “hot” mid-sentence. Turning moves the cursor, a word at a time when spun.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: How a chat opens: the field is focused but inactive, with no cursor. Backspace leaves and keeps the draft; typing or Enter
activates it, cursor where it was left. Turning goes up into the messages.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: With focus in the messages the composer folds to one line, giving the history most of the screen. Turning down past the newest

g.text: Hut is open and the stove works. Water
from the spring is fine if you filter it. Snow
starts about 200 m above the hut, so
leave the trail runners and bring boots.
The bunk room sleeps six; we have four,
so there is room for you and Sam. Radio
check at 19:00 on the usual channel.
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: A message taller than the view scrolls line by line while focused, its cut edges showing there is more; focus moves on only once
its last line is in view.

g.text: are with me; Lee went back to move the truck.
We have water and the spare radio, and I will
check in again from the saddle

svg.text: The composer grows upward to three lines; past that it scrolls within itself to follow the cursor, and the bar shows where.
Sideways scrolling would hide the start of the message.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: Pressing a focused message opens what the iOS long-press gives, reactions first. Typing closes the menu and goes to the

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: A chip over the bubble’s outer top corner, as on iOS: top-left on a sent message, top-right on a received one, gray when it is
From Details. The rows of the iOS sheet that a reader on a communicator needs; the list continues to the source check. Delivery
state lives under the bubble, not here.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam says…

svg.text: The quoted message sits above the composer. Backspace only erases while typing; after Done, the first Backspace drops the
reply and keeps the text, the next leaves.
The unconfirmed message is focused and pressed to retry. When airtime is spent, the composer keeps the draft and says when
Send returns, inline rather than in an alert.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: Banners are passive. They never take a key, so Enter still sends the draft they interrupted. A haptic tick, then it times out; the
chat waits at the top of Chats.
After an hour’s quiet, a separator says when the conversation picked up again: the day, then the time, as on iOS. Today,
Yesterday, a weekday within the week, then the date. Each message’s own time is in Details.
A reply quotes the start of the message it answers, with its sender, at the top of its bubble, as the composer’s strip does while you
write one. When the answered message is not here, the reply shows without a quote.
An edited message shows its new text and says so under the bubble. A deleted one leaves a line in its place, with no bubble,

g.text: Try the valley from the saddle

svg.text: A message missing from the sequence has been asked for again. The typing dots hold its place until it comes, so it lands where it
was sent rather than at the end.

g.text: It covers the north side now

svg.text: Above, the missing message came and fills its slot, marked late. Below, its sender could no longer supply the next one, and a line

g.text: How is the trail past the creek?

svg.text: A long message shows as its parts arrive. The dots count them, filled as each comes in, and the ellipsis marks where the rest will

g.text: How is the trail past the creek?

svg.text: A part that never came: the message is shown without it, the ellipsis and its dot turn amber, and the message no longer waits.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: In a chat that holds a session with forward secrecy, the composer is violet while you edit: what it sends goes under the session.
Not typing, it is the usual blue.

g.text: Can you grab the big map?

svg.text: A message sent while the composer was violet stays violet, and a reply’s quote takes its tints. Those sent before the session stay

g.text: On my way, save me some hot

svg.text: Pressing an unconfirmed violet message asks how to send it again. Try again keeps forward secrecy; only the second choice
sends without it, and the message turns blue. Backspace cancels.
Sender label and avatar on each run, by the iOS authority order; an unidentified member shows its hint. Group sends end at
A member’s message adds View member, the way to reach someone you have only heard in a channel.
Matching reactions share a chip with a count. Yours takes the bubble color and sits in front at the corner, with the cluster’s one
A channel message carries only a hint. Request identity asks over the channel; when the identity arrives the address fills in and

g.text: Which channel is the crew on?

svg.text: An invitation link renders as a card, since a link inside text cannot take focus. Pressing it opens the actions with Join Trail Crew

g.text: Anyone with this invite can read and post.

svg.text: The invitation’s preview. Nothing is joined or sent until Join channel. Region and hops from the link apply silently, as on iOS.

g.text: Anyone with this card can read and post.

svg.text: Boards with NFC. A tag carrying a channel invitation opens the same screen; the warning names the card, since a card can be
Device › Channels › Add channel. One field takes a channel name or a umsh:ck: invitation, and the preview says which as you
type. A name is short; a key is the painful case shown.
Joined from the start. Traffic is signed and unencrypted, so every sender is named and anyone in range can read it. It alerts like
Backspace from a top-level list lands on the rail; turning switches lists live, press enters. Add peer heads the list.
Opens on Nearby: devices that also have Add peer open, nearest first, by model and a color that is new each time the screen
opens. No name, address or avatar is sent or shown until both people confirm the code. You is this device’s color. The arcs show
how close; the back-to-back glyph shows only on boards with NFC.
Pat’s T-Deck, drawn at the Pager’s size, when Juniper presses its row. Pat knows who asked by who is standing there. Not now

g.text: Same code on the other screen?

svg.text: Both screens show the same six digits only if nobody is in the middle. Names still have not been sent. Turning moves between

g.text: Same code on the other screen?

svg.text: After Same, until the other side presses Same too. Then both devices send their addresses and names, save each other, and
open the peer’s page with Message focused. Leaving here cancels.
Either side pressing Different lands both here, with nothing sent and nothing saved. Try again goes back to Nearby.
Boards with NFC. Holding two devices back to back, both on Add peer, exchanges contacts with no code: the touch is the
agreement. Both land here, saved. Forget on the peer’s page undoes a mistaken tap.
Add peer › Enter an address. Takes a 44-character address or a umsh:n: invitation. The address wraps at a fixed column; the
avatar appears from the first characters, and Message unlocks when it is complete.
The full address fits on one line. One focusable list of readouts and actions follows; Forget is last and asks to confirm. Share
contact sends the peer to a chat.
A version-4 QR at about 5 px per module, sized for scanning rather than type. Turning on Shows switches between the identity
and joined channels. The pattern is illustrative. On boards with NFC, a phone tapping the device while this is open reads the
same link; Add peer never serves it.
A message whose whole body is a umsh:n: link renders as a contact card, as invites do for channels. Pressing it opens the peer’s
Says who sent the contact. Save peer keeps it; Message works without saving.
From a peer’s page. Picks a chat; the contact goes there as an ordinary message.
Settings drill down: categories with a one-word summary, press to enter. Radio detail lives here too, since the radio is built in.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam
On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: A passive banner, like a message’s, and the strip’s battery turns amber. It does not take a key or cover the composer.
The last thing shown before the power path opens: the empty battery blinks a few times, then the panel goes dark. No words to
The identity exists before this screen. The name is optional: Continue with it empty and peers see the bare hint.
Required before the first transmission, since it sets what the radio may use. The same list is Device › Radio later.
Asked even with a GNSS fix, which gives the time but not the zone. The list starts on the zone set, UTC until now; letters narrow
it. Device › Clock › Time zone later.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam

svg.text: Shift arms itself where a sentence starts, shown by the outlined arrow in the strip. The next letter is a capital; tapping Shift instead

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam

svg.text: “hut” then two quick spaces typed “hut. ”, and Shift armed for the next sentence. Only when the key before the first space was
a letter; moving the cursor in between breaks the sequence.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam

svg.text: Shift tapped twice quickly, or Alt then Shift. The filled arrow with a bar stays until Shift or Alt is tapped.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam

svg.text: Alt tapped once: the next key types its orange legend, here about to type “?”, and Alt disarms. Held instead, Alt applies while it is
down and the strip shows nothing.
A numeric field opens in symbol lock, so the top row types digits and Alt+F the minus sign. Space types a space. No capitalizing

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam

svg.text: Alt+Space. Turning walks the grid and its categories in order; press inserts at the cursor and closes. Backspace closes without
inserting. The third row is clipped: the grid goes on.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam

svg.text: Letters typed in the picker filter it by name, in place of the category row.

g.text: At the north junction yet? Sam

svg.text: Space while the picker is open toggles the keyboard light and closes the picker, so Alt+Space, Space is the light switch.

g.text: On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: Holding Alt down while turning the wheel sets the screen brightness. Only a held Alt: a one-shot or locked Alt leaves the wheel to
Device › Keyboard. The two typing aids can be turned off everywhere; fields that never want them turn them off for themselves.

g.text: Are you on the ridge yet?
Sam: Will wait 10 min at t…
Road is open past the gate
Scroll down and press to unlock

svg.text: A key or a small turn lights a locked device to this. So does every message that would alert, with the haptic tick, its card landing
on top and the 15 s starting over. One card per chat heard from since locking; the badge counts unread chats.

g.text: Are you on the ridge yet?
Sam: Will wait 10 min at t…
Road is open past the gate
Scroll down and press to unlock

svg.text: Turning down fills the bar, five steps to the mark; turning up empties it. The cards stay put: the wheel only feeds the bar. Pressing
before the bar is full does nothing.

g.text: Are you on the ridge yet?
Sam: Will wait 10 min at t…
Road is open past the gate

svg.text: Past the mark the bar turns green and the hint changes. A press within 2 s unlocks, back to where you were, with the cards’ chats
at the top of Chats; otherwise the bar empties and it starts over.

g.text: Scroll down and press to unlock

svg.text: With no cards, the time takes the middle. While charging, the charge shows under the date. After 15 s the screen fades, then
goes dark, sooner than when unlocked.

g.text: Are you on the ridge yet?
Sam: Will wait 10 min at t…
Road is open past the gate
Scroll down and press to unlock

svg.text: Until the clock is known, no time or date shows anywhere: not here, in the strip, or in Details. Ages of messages heard since
power-on are measured, not read off the clock, so they stay.
Device › Clock. Set automatically takes the time from GNSS, or from the phone when linked; Date and time is then a readout.
Last set from says where the time came from, and when.
With Set automatically off. Turning moves between the parts; pressing one lets turning change it, and digits type it. Set starts the
Zones by name, west to east, with today’s offset, daylight saving included. Letters filter the list, as on every list.

g.text: On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: A press opens a chat when the wheel comes back up; holding it down opens the chat’s menu instead. A channel’s says Show

g.text: On my way, save me some hot coffee

svg.text: Asks to confirm, Cancel focused, as Forget does. The chat and its messages go; the peer stays saved, and their next message
Each modifier is off, one-shot or locked. Held down, either applies only while it is down and changes no state.
The lock button is the one at the bottom edge, also the bootloader button. A password, later, would follow the press.
Turn moves, press selects, Backspace goes back. No text field is involved, so Backspace is always Back.
Turn to Radio; press to open it. Its summary shows the current preset.
Radio opens as its own screen. Turn to Preset; press to change it.
The choices open in place, the current one checked. Turn to Medium
range; press to choose. Backspace cancels.
Preset reads Medium range. Turn to Share location; press flips the
switch. Changes apply at once; there is no Save.
Backspace steps back out to the categories; a second Backspace goes
